slides.title: Grief & Loss: The Grief Process
text: Denial – The client has difficulty believing a terminal diagnosis or loss.
Anger – Anger is directed toward self, others, or objects.
Bargaining – The client negotiates for more time or a cure.
Depression – The client mourns and directly confronts feelings related to the loss.
Acceptance – The client accepts what is happening and plans for the future.

slides.title: A paranoid client reports that men in blue clothing keep looking in the window and whispering. Which of the following responses by the nurse is most appropriate?
text: A paranoid client reports that men in blue clothing keep looking in the window and whispering. Which of the following responses by the nurse is most appropriate?
“Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.”
“Do not take things personally, not everyone who is whispering is whispering about you.”
“Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.”
“I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.”

slides.title: “Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.” Yes, the nurse does not want to agree with the client. They should be truthful and matter of fact.
text: “Those men are groundskeepers. They are talking about their work, not you.” Yes, the nurse does not want to agree with the client. They should be truthful and matter of fact.
“Do not take things personally, not everyone who is talking is talking about you.” No, this disregards the clients thought and appears condescending.
“Do not pay attention to the men. Shall we play cards instead.” No, this is distraction and the client will still have the same thoughts.
“I will close the drapes so you can't see the men.” No, this does not address the false thoughts of the client.
